note: RFC 6811 Section 2 requires the Route's validation state to reflect the lookup result. The lookup uses the final AS_PATH segment: a final AS_SEQUENCE supplies its rightmost AS, an empty or confederation-ending path uses the local speaker AS, and AS_SET supplies NONE. TestValidateValid and TestValidateInvalid use the same covered prefix with respectively authorized and unauthorized origins and assert the exact Valid and Invalid constants. TestRouteStateIsSetFromTheLookup drives validateNLRIs for independently expected Valid, Invalid and NotFound results and checks both the returned per-prefix state and the queued decision state; its second arm performs a changed lookup and requires Invalid instead of the earlier Valid. TestBatchValidateTypedMatchesString retains every original typed-versus-text parity assertion and now also requires each transport to settle all four pending inputs, retain exactly the two accepted keys with their absolute Valid and Invalid states, and omit the two explicitly discarded keys. An accepted Invalid lookup therefore cannot become Valid merely because policy accepted it, and a shared wrong state or empty result on both transports cannot pass. TestRPKIOriginASFromASPathRFC6811 retains empty, sequence, set and confederation controls and adds distinct first/final sequence values plus a sequence followed by a final AS_SET. These require final-segment selection and NONE rather than an AS_SET member. Source review traces validateNLRIs, handleBatchValidateTyped, batchValidateCommand, applyDecision and promoteToInstalled, together with ROACache.Validate and rpkiOriginASFromASPath. The five new native clean runs in job-rpki-origin-existing-native-proofs-e302411f.log passed their named tests. Normal-return producer faults then failed the intended exact assertions: forcing promotion to Valid changed both transports' accepted Invalid state from 3 to 1; reversing the Valid and Invalid lookup returns failed their respective lookup tests; selecting the first segment failed only the two new multisegment cases; using an AS_SET member as origin failed both final-set cases while empty, sequence and confederation controls passed. The seven canonical records comprise those five semantic observations and the two earlier validateNLRIs boundary-disable observations; the latter prove boundary reachability, while the test's exact expected-state assertions supply the semantic checks. The current production delivery contract is not a flattened JSON path: runRPKIPlugin subscribes to full events, handleStructuredUpdate uses segment-bearing attributes, handleEvent prefers raw attribute bytes or hex and uses the same segment-aware helper, and configuration revalidation decodes retained raw attributes before its lookup. Supplied malformed raw attributes do not fall back to the flattened path. Source also implements AS_CONFED_SET through the same local-AS branch as AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE; the existing untagged TestJSONOriginUsesLocalASAndRawSegmentTypes checks both confederation forms, empty path and AS_SET for byte and hex event forms. Those supporting tests are not counted as additional tagged discrimination records. Only the no-raw compatibility projection lacks segment types and uses the flattened path; this audit does not claim that projection can reconstruct information it never carries. The enforced verdict is for the stated MUST that a performed lookup's result becomes the route's state, with origin selection and acceptance-preservation assertions protecting that result. It does not certify every compatibility input, policy defaults or policy assignment, mapping-deletion revalidation, every address-family delivery path, or whole-RFC support; those are separate obligations and evidence. The earlier blanket claim that the normal JSON route necessarily misclassifies AS_SET or confederation origins is contradicted by the current full-event subscription and raw-attribute producers and is not retained.
